# `prefer-split-scalar`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports `std.mem.splitSequence`, `std.mem.splitBackwardsSequence`,
`std.mem.tokenizeSequence`, or `std.mem.tokenizeAny` called with a
single-character string literal instead of using `splitScalar`,
`splitBackwardsScalar`, or `tokenizeScalar` with a character literal.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Splitting or tokenizing by a single delimiter using sequence-based iterators
incurs the overhead of multi-byte slice matching. Zig's standard library
provides specialized scalar iterators (`splitScalar`, `splitBackwardsScalar`,
`tokenizeScalar`) that scan for individual characters directly, producing faster
code with less register pressure.

## When it fires

Whenever splitting lines, CSV columns, path components, or words by a single
delimiter character.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn firstField(line: []const u8) ?[]const u8 {
    var parts = std.mem.splitSequence(u8, line, ",");
    return parts.next();
}
```
